## First incorrect owners and minimal repairs

There are five independently demonstrated first-owner defects across four
mechanisms (the two binding resolvers implement the same stack-growth mechanism
in different engines). No count is attributed to historical controls.

1. **Rust demanded-binding native recursion.** Prior checkpoint evidence shows
   Base C3 abort and safe eight-diamond depth17 despite exact result31. Existing
   `evaluation/scalars/bindings.rs` now drives demanded initializer continuations
   on heap; `expression_evaluator.rs` retains its existing iterative AST frames
   until the dependency is ready. Corrected depth2, shared initialization once,
   lazy branches, missing/cycle diagnostics and transient geometry recovery are
   covered. This continuation's source-backed R1 and complete C3 PASS discharge
   the earlier incomplete source/runtime acceptance. No destructive removal run.
2. **TS demanded-binding native recursion.** Existing `declarationEvaluator.ts`
   retained a native call per binding through `evaluateTypedExpression` and
   lookupBinding. R1 has shallow individual ASTs, Root7 and eight serial
   diamonds, independently Join_i=7+3(i+1), Join7=31. All25 values pass on Base
   but actual resolver frames reach17 and the <=2 assertion fails. The existing
   resolver now owns heap pending frames; `expressionEvaluator.ts` uses generator
   continuations of its existing operations. Only reached lookups suspend.
   Stable memoization remains per evaluator; transient request results clear
   between geometry-state views. Result insertion order, local/match/record/map
   scopes and callbacks are covered. Safe two-file Base removal again gives
   depth17/FAIL; corrected depth2/PASS. There is no alternate scheduler, eager
   inactive evaluation or RangeError catch.
3. **Rust empty readiness queries rebuilt/scanned topology.** Three exact Base
   B1:B2 paired blocks give persistent Rust medians about55/617–638ms, ratio
   11.3–11.6 for graph V+E396→1548. Native sampling attributes451/579 evaluation
   samples to ready_dependency_scheduled_binding_ids rebuilding maps for no
   candidates. R2's compiler-emitted graph has29 edges. Empty candidate queries
   visit464 edges; empty-error prerequisite queries visit232; answers are empty
   or false throughout. Adjacent empty graph passes. Three early returns in
   `evaluation/conditional_dependency_runtime.rs` avoid work only when the exact
   answer follows from an empty query/error set. Nonempty error propagation and
   candidates retain existing implementation. Removal reproduces464/232 FAIL;
   corrected both0 PASS. Test-only counters record actual edge visits.
4. **Compiler computed discarded automatic names.** Repeated Base-compiler
   B2:B3 p50 about56/543–554ms plus V8 CPU stacks identify elementNames called
   from actual source insertion through createCadElement. The compiler replaces
   that interactive name with the already validated authored name. R3 keeps ten
   authored geometry names exact but Base makes18 automatic computations over a
   growing namespace. The main DSL insertion passes the authored name to the
   existing factory; the factory bypasses only automatic naming. Reference/default
   construction logic and ordinary interactive naming remain unchanged. R3 uses
   the same small legal source as R2 for a different independent owner probe;

   gives18 FAIL while ordinary UI naming passes; corrected0 PASS.
5. **Numeric lowering multiplied elements by all bindings.** Three Base-owner
   D2:D3 lowering blocks p50 about1.4–1.5/18.2–18.9ms, V8 profile and loop
   inspection identify the Cartesian scan in numericBindingRuntime.ts. R4 has

   entries still follows statement-map order, then original per-statement binding

## Performance protocol and limits

See `performance-summary.md`, `performance-normalized.json` and losslessly
archived raw JSON/profiles. Eighteen frozen comparisons use five warmups and21
alternating paired trials, one persistent child, normal production lowering,
separate cold/build setup, source/payload bytes, V/E, worker CPU per stage,
child batch CPU/RSS and p50/p95/max. JSON encoding is an additional probe; Rust
transport already includes real encode/JSON decode and cannot be summed with
that probe. Result decoding is measured separately. CPU from ps has0.01s batch
resolution and is not fabricated into per-request Rust CPU. Restoration is
verified by the full correctness transition suite; paired edit/permutation
measurements compare initial and changed canonical revisions.

Performance baseline provenance is explicit: exact Base Rust binary was built
in a separate target directory after temporarily restoring only the three
previously changed Rust files and proving every Rust source matched Base, then
restoring candidate files byte-for-byte. No checkout was created. Only safe
B1/B2 (plus cold A1) were evaluated on this binary. Compiler baseline imports
only unchanged Base Language Core; lowering baseline isolates the unchanged
numeric owner/production lowering before that repair. These stage-isolated
measurements are not a claim of a full unsafe Base C3 timing run. Three clean
paired blocks precede separately profiled fourth blocks. Final full campaign
reruns every contaminated cell on the combined candidate.

The earlier120s B2:B3 grouping deadline was a harness batch-size failure:
individual requests kept progressing below15s with no exhaustion/hang/unsafe
teardown. The same21-pair order was split into seven bounded three-pair tests;
per-request/case resource limits were not raised. Initial evidence is retained.
Source/test helper corrections (canonical ID setup, trace display depth,
constructor-spy prototype, unsupported helper syntax) are retained as harness
